quarterly_data.signal: Q2 FY2026 results (December quarter): revenue was a record $1.69 billion, up 7% sequentially and 17% year over year, driven by AI data center and communications demand (pro forma, excluding the divested aerospace and defense business: up 9% sequentially and 22% year over year). Non-GAAP gross margin was 39% (up 24 basis points sequentially and 77 basis points year over year), non-GAAP operating margin 19.9%, and non-GAAP EPS $1.29 versus $1.16 in the prior quarter and $0.95 a year ago. The Data Center and Communications segment, now over 70% of revenue, grew 11% sequentially and 34% year over year; within it the data center business grew 14% sequentially and 36% year over year on growth in both 800G and 1.6T transceivers, and communications grew 9% sequentially and 44% year over year.
quarterly_data.figure: record $1.69 billion revenue, up 7% sequentially and 17% year over year; 39% non-GAAP gross margin; $1.29 non-GAAP EPS; data center up 14% sequentially and 36% year over year

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 FY2026 (March quarter) guidance: revenue between $1.7 billion and $1.84 billion (including $5 million of revenue from the Munich product division before its sale closed), non-GAAP gross margin between 38.5% and 40.5%, non-GAAP operating expenses between $320 million and $340 million, and non-GAAP EPS between $1.28 and $1.48. Management expects double-digit sequential data center growth in both the March and June quarters, continued strong sequential company revenue growth in both quarters, a fiscal 2027 revenue growth rate above fiscal 2026's, and EPS growing significantly faster than revenue. Named growth drivers: 800G and 1.6T transceivers, the ramps of new OCS and CPO products, and very strong DCI/scale-across demand.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue between $1.7 billion and $1.84 billion; non-GAAP gross margin between 38.5% and 40.5%; non-GAAP EPS between $1.28 and $1.48

quarterly_data.signal: Data center bookings took another step-function increase in Q2, with a book-to-bill ratio that exceeded 4x; the vast majority came from 800G and 1.6T transceiver bookings (1.6T accelerating), with OCS also contributing, and management expects another very strong bookings quarter. Most of calendar 2026 is already booked out and most new bookings are now for calendar 2027; large customers provide detailed forecasts out into calendar 2028. Coherent has signed, or is signing, long-term supply agreements in which it guarantees supply, customers guarantee demand, and customers often make financial commitments such as CapEx investment. Management said the visibility of the business is 'the best it's ever been'.
quarterly_data.figure: data center book-to-bill exceeded 4x; most of calendar '26 booked out; customer forecasts into calendar '28

quarterly_data.signal: Six-inch indium phosphide ramp running ahead of plan: Coherent significantly increased InP production in Q2 and is on track to double internal InP production by the fourth quarter of calendar 2026. Current-quarter wafer starts are already at 80% of the doubling target, after wafer starts more than quadrupled from the September quarter to the December quarter; a wafer start takes about six months to become a transceiver shipment, so the benefit starts this quarter and builds over coming quarters. Production is ramping in parallel at Sherman, Texas and Yarfala, Sweden, with EMLs, CW lasers and photodiodes all in production on six-inch and six-inch yields exceeding three-inch yields. A six-inch wafer produces more than four times as many chips at less than half the cost; almost all capacity being added is six-inch, about half of capacity will be six-inch by the end of calendar 2026, and plans go well beyond doubling in following years. Coherent has multiple six-inch InP substrate suppliers and has secured committed substrate supply supporting the doubling; management called Coherent the world's only producer of six-inch indium phosphide.
quarterly_data.figure: wafer starts at 80% of the capacity-doubling target; about six months from wafer start to transceiver shipment

quarterly_data.signal: Management does not foresee indium phosphide supply and demand getting back in balance this calendar year or next calendar year, and, given customer forecasts for the InP laser supply they need for scale-up, sees a possible 'very sustained long period of supply-demand imbalance on indium phosphide'; customer demand absorbs all planned capacity 'and then some'. The majority of Coherent's InP lasers are internally sourced and the internal share is expected to grow, but external EML supply increased sequentially in Q2 and is expected to increase again through long-term partnerships with key external suppliers (kept for customer and supply-chain resiliency reasons). Coherent is seeing higher input pricing on externally sourced EMLs, which management said is offset by its internal InP ramp for a net positive, and it continues to optimize its own pricing in the strong demand environment.

Coherent recently secured an 'exceptionally large' purchase order from a market-leading AI data center customer (not named) for a CPO solution that includes its new high-power CW laser, which began sampling last year; a key factor in the customer's choice was that the laser is produced on the six-inch InP line in Sherman, Texas (US-based manufacturing). Initial revenue is expected toward the end of calendar 2026, with a more significant contribution next calendar year and beyond. The solution will initially be deployed in scale-out and is expected to lead to scale-up deployments over time. On top of transceiver demand, Coherent is ramping InP capacity to support the high-power CW laser demand ahead, and it has engagements with multiple other customers for InP- and 200G VCSEL-based solutions for CPO and MPO applications.

Management views CPO as additive: pluggable transceivers remain the dominant form factor in scale-across and scale-out through at least the rest of the decade, CPO deploys first in scale-out, but the big CPO growth is driven by scale-up, which management believes 'will dwarf the opportunity in scale-out' and be 'orders of magnitude larger', all incremental TAM because the in-rack scale-up network is 100% electrical today. There are very active, deep CPO design-win engagements for scale-up across multiple customers, and management does not consider scale-up CPO years out. Coherent plans to supply scale-up both at the component level (high-power CW lasers, detectors, fiber optical cable) and at higher levels (external laser sources, including pluggable laser sources for the front panel, and CPO module assemblies).

OCS (optical circuit switch on Coherent's non-mechanical liquid crystal technology): backlog grew sequentially in Q2 and Coherent now has over 10 customer engagements; shipments and backlog include 64 by 64 and 320 by 320 system sizes, with most backlog weighted toward the larger size. OCS revenue is expected to grow sequentially this quarter and ramp through this calendar year and into next year, with Coherent 100% focused on ramping production. Applications are broadening from spine/redundancy and scale-out uses to the DC portion of the network and to scale-up; the market sized about a year ago at about $2 billion by the end of the decade was likely undersized and, if reassessed now, would be well above $2 billion.
quarterly_data.figure: over 10 customer engagements; addressable market well above $2 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Communications (DCI, scale-across and traditional telecom): extremely strong demand for data center interconnect products, including ZR and ZR+ coherent transceivers and lasers and other components sold to system OEMs, with DCI growing faster than the overall communications business and backlog growing. Coherent recently secured a significant multiyear design win with a leading DCI OEM (not named) that uses its industry-first uncooled three-pin micropump solution. The new multi-rail platform, which lets network operators get more traffic through existing optical infrastructure, has design wins and orders, with revenue contribution expected to start in the second half of calendar 2026. Communications is expected to grow sequentially in the March and June quarters.

Q2 capital expenditures were $154 million versus $104 million in the prior quarter and $106 million a year ago, and are expected to increase sequentially over the remainder of fiscal 2026 as Coherent rapidly expands capacity for data center and communications demand. Beyond InP, it is expanding transceiver assembly and test capacity: a second facility in Penang, Malaysia was opened, and Vietnam, which already makes transceiver components, is starting to build transceivers; DCI and telecom capacity is also being expanded. Coherent uses outsourcing partners and keeps in-house only what gives a technology or cost-structure advantage.
quarterly_data.figure: $154 million Q2 capex vs $104 million prior quarter and $106 million year-ago quarter

quarterly_data.signal: 800G is still the biggest portion of Coherent's transceiver revenue and is expected to grow year over year in calendar 2026; both 800G and 1.6T grew in Q2 and are expected to grow again in the March quarter. 800G bookings came in a little stronger than expected and, together with 1.6T, made up the vast majority of Q2 data center bookings (book-to-bill above 4x). The six-inch InP capacity ramp supports both 800G and 1.6T transceivers and is a gross margin driver for the transceiver business.

The 1.6T transceiver ramp has accelerated with demand, with Coherent ramping at multiple customers and seeing a 'tremendous amount of orders' on 1.6T. The early phase of the ramp is driven by Coherent's EML-based and silicon photonics-based 1.6T transceivers (both ramping; the mix follows the customer application, with no big financial difference between them), followed by 200 gig VCSEL-based 1.6T transceivers ramping in the second half of calendar 2026. 1.6T is growing much faster than 800G off a smaller base and will keep ramping into the following calendar year. 1.6T ASPs are higher than 800G and 1.6T gross margins are expected to be higher, so management views the ramp as margin accretive.
quarterly_data.figure: EML and silicon photonics 1.6T ramping first; 200 gig VCSEL-based 1.6T ramps in the second half of calendar 2026
